source.title: Generalization Error Bounds for Deep Neural Networks Trained by SGD

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The experiments measure cumulative loss (CL), a component of the paper’s proposed generalization bound, across label-noise, class-count, and network-size conditions. They do not measure test error or the train–test gap directly.
record.gate_note: The reported experiments measure CL, not test error or the train–test gap. No results test the listed versions directly; CL is recorded as a proposed generalization-related measure. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study derives generalization bounds and measures cumulative loss (CL), rather than testing any listed version. Label-noise experiments report neither fitting accuracy nor held-out accuracy; network-size experiments vary VGG depth and report CL rather than test error. Width experiments measure bound sensitivity, not generalization past interpolation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they derive trajectory-dependent bounds for deep FNNs and CNNs trained by GF, GD or SGD, and describe their numerical bounds as non-vacuous and robust. They interpret increasing CL with noise and class count, and its overall negative association with VGG size, as reflecting generalization ability. That interpretation is not validated by paired held-out-performance measurements in Table 2, and the VGG-size trend is not monotonic.
record.recipe_differences: The paper derives and evaluates generalization bounds using parameter norms and cumulative loss; it does not reproduce the original empirical interventions or measures in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported CL changes with label-noise proportion, number of classes, and network size. The paper also says its bounds are not sensitive to changes in width and learning rate in the bound-focused experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: VGG-16 CL increases from 6.60 to 62.65 across the reported label-noise proportions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing label noise increases the cumulative-loss component of this bound in the tested binary CIFAR-10 setting.

fits_no_version.finding: VGG-16 CL increases from 6.60 to 26.08 as the number of classes increases from two to ten.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CL increases with class count in the tested CIFAR-10 subsets.

fits_no_version.finding: CL is 15.51, 9.52, 6.60 and 7.88 for VGG-11, VGG-13, VGG-16 and VGG-19.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CL generally decreases across the tested VGG depths, with an increase at VGG-19; this does not establish lower test error.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 7.1 reports slowly growing bounds and low sensitivity of the bounds to width and learning rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed generalization bounds are numerically stable under the tested hyperparameter changes.

record.problems: The reported large-scale experiments provide CL values but no test-error or train–test-gap values, so they do not directly validate CL as a measure of those quantities. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the table values.
record.rows_left_out: None; all 13 Table 2 CL values are recorded separately.

untested.parts: Coexistence of near-perfect random-label fitting and natural-label generalization, including chance held-out accuracy with random labels.
Test-error changes when width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Held-out performance comparisons between convolutional and fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on held-out performance under different tuning recipes.
Large-batch held-out performance penalties under fixed epoch budgets and their recovery through recipe changes.
Effects of dropout, training-set size, augmentation and weight decay on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with measured generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples compared with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All 13 CL values match Table 2. CL is a functional of training loss, not held-out error, a measured generalization gap or magnitude-aware sharpness. Theoretical upper bounds alone do not establish the empirical comparisons specified by V1–V8. Repeated table conditions should not count as independent evidence.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not compare fitting natural labels with fitting random labels or report held-out accuracy for either.
The paper does not sweep width past the interpolation threshold or report test error across widths.
The paper does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks on image test error.
The paper does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out performance.
The paper does not compare batch sizes or report their effect on held-out performance.
The paper does not test dropout or its effect on held-out error.
The paper does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with generalization gaps.
The paper does not remove memorized examples or measure the resulting test accuracy.
